direct_question:
Audit the CURRENT refactored intake for completeness, not just documents. Can we make an accurate eligibility screening conclusion from these answers? List all missing facts, conditional visibility failures, precision gaps, program-specific eligibility-unit inputs, and mandatory unresolved criteria. Include concise simple followup wording and exactly when to ask it. Separate criteria facts from application paperwork.
What external documents would possibly be needed, and what rules/triggers necessitate them? Give a concrete document-to-question matrix for your program. Show questions already in our intake, questions needing further detail, and questions belonging in the actual application session. Assess whether our intake supports accurate preliminary eligibility conclusions. Retrieve official sources before answering.

mappings.document_name: Medicare Savings Program policy (CMS Chapter 1) — verification rules (income/resources, citizenship, AVS/self-attestation)
mappings.question: Is the applicant’s household income and resources below MSP thresholds; are they enrolled in Medicare Part A or B; is the applicant a U.S. citizen or satisfactory immigration status?
mappings.subject_and_period: Current monthly income and resources (most recent month / 12‑month lookback only if state requires), Medicare enrollment status (current), citizenship/immigration declaration (current)
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Do you or the person you care for have Medicare Part A or B? Which parts and what are the claim/Medicare numbers? (If unknown, choose 'I'm not sure')
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: States determine MSP eligibility using income and resource limits (see Appendix 1.A); CMS requires states to accept self-attestation for interest/dividend income and non‑liquid resources, but states may use AVS or request documentation; states must obtain a signed declaration of citizenship or satisfactory immigration status (if returned signed, US citizens need not be further verified).
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: Any screening for MSPs or when user goal includes 'Medical coverage' or when recipient.current_benefits includes Medicare
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: If self-attestation is ambiguous or state requires verification, or applicant indicates resources/assets that may be countable (e.g., savings/investments, life insurance cash value), or user indicates Medicaid application pending/denied
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Yes for many MSP-counted items per CMS (self-attestation acceptable for interest/dividend income and non-liquid resources); Medicare enrollment must be self-reported for screening but agency will verify
alternatives: Self-reported Medicare part enrollment and income ranges for preliminary screen; agency verification via AVS or benefit letters at application
mappings.requirement_support: CMS MSP Chapter 1 — self-attestation acceptance, citizenship declaration requirement, Appendix 1.A income/resource categories
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: Applies nationally to MSPs; states may implement AVS or additional procedures by April 1, 2026 as noted in CMS doc
mappings.review_notes: Intake collects rough monthly income ranges and household size (recipient.monthly_income_range, recipient.household_size) but lacks Medicare Part A/B enrollment and citizenship/immigration declaration questions; resource detail and spouse income not captured.

mappings.document_name: Medicare & You — MSP overview and state variability
mappings.question: Does the state offer QMB/SLMB/QI and what benefits would the recipient get if eligible?
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Which state Medicaid/medical assistance office handles MSPs for [recipient.address.state]? (We can look this up if you want.)
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: MSP names, income/resource limits, and benefits vary by state; applicants should contact state Medicaid office or apply through state process. Preliminary screening must treat MSPs as state‑specific.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: Any interest in help paying Medicare (case.goals includes 'Medical coverage') or mention of Medicare
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: When preparing to recommend an application path or forms, lookup state's MSP program page
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Yes to determine whether the person appears to fall into a national income/resource band, but state lookup required for exact thresholds and forms
alternatives: Self-report eligibility flags; staff lookup of state MSP names and thresholds
mappings.requirement_support: Medicare & You explains MSPs are state-administered and thresholds vary
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: State variations important; this is national guidance
mappings.review_notes: Intake does not capture state-specific program names or acceptance options for MSPs; needs a step to resolve state thresholds before application.

mappings.document_name: CMS MSP Chapter 1 — Asset Verification System (AVS) and what states may require
mappings.question: Does the applicant have countable resources (bank balances, cash value of life insurance, burial funds) and can they self-attest, or will the state need AVS verification?
mappings.subject_and_period: Current resources and value; burial set-asides; life insurance cash value (current)
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Please list the types of assets owned (savings, investment accounts, life insurance with cash value, property other than primary home). Do you know approximate values?
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: CMS requires states to either accept self-attestation of non-liquid resources and interest/dividend income or use AVS; states may require documentary proof if AVS or other verification fails. Burial funds treated differently between LIS and MSPs.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: When resources are reported (recipient.assets not 'None') or the recipient is applying for MSPs
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: If user cannot self-attest values or state indicates AVS will be used, request bank statements, life insurance statements, property deeds at application/agency followup
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Yes for many items (CMS says self-attestation acceptable), but if applicant reports high/uncertain assets, agency may require documentation
alternatives: Self-attestation for preliminary screen; request documents only if necessary at application
mappings.requirement_support: CMS MSP Chapter 1 sections on verification and AVS
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: Applies nationally but states choose AVS vs self-attestation implementation
mappings.review_notes: Intake asks asset types but not values, spouse assets or burial funds; no direct question on life insurance cash value — gap for MSP countable resources.

mappings.document_name: CMS MSP Chapter 1 — Citizenship/Immigration declaration rules
mappings.question: Is the applicant a U.S. citizen or do they have satisfactory immigration status? Has the applicant signed the required declaration?
mappings.subject_and_period: Current citizenship/immigration status; signed declaration at application
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Are you or the person you care for a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or a non‑citizen with satisfactory immigration status? (This is required for MSP/Medicaid application.)
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: States must request a signed declaration of U.S. citizenship or satisfactory immigration status; if citizen returns signed declaration, no further verification required. Non‑citizens may require immigration documentation.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: When screening for MSPs or full Medicaid benefits
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: If non‑citizen or citizenship uncertain, agency will request immigration documents (USCIS forms, green card, naturalization certificate) at application
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Self-report is sufficient to screen preliminarily; signed declaration and documentary evidence may be required at application
alternatives: Self-report for screening; declaration and agency verification for application
mappings.requirement_support: CMS MSP Chapter 1 citizenship verification section
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: Applies to MSPs nationally; state procedures for non‑citizens vary
mappings.review_notes: Intake lacks any citizenship/immigration question — mandatory omission for MSP/Medicaid screening.

mappings.document_name: CMS MSP Chapter 1 Appendix 1.A — income/resource categories & thresholds (reference)
mappings.question: Does reported household income fall into QMB/SLMB/QI eligibility ranges once household size and unearned/in-kind rules are applied?
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Please provide monthly gross and net income amounts for the recipient and their spouse (if applicable) and indicate which household members contribute income.
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: MSP groups are defined by FPL percentages and resource limits that depend on household size; family size rules can affect eligibility and require precise household composition (see CMS memo referenced in Chapter 1).
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: When recipient.monthly_income_range indicates low-income or when case.goals include MSP assistance
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: If income range ambiguous or near thresholds, request paystubs, benefit letters, or tax returns during application or to verify
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: A monthly income range may be sufficient to place a person in a likely MSP band for preliminary recommendations, but precise dollar amounts and household composition are needed for a defensible eligibility conclusion
alternatives: Self-reported ranges for preliminary screen; exact paystubs/SSA award letters for application verification
mappings.requirement_support: CMS Appendix 1.A provides income/resource banding and how coverage corresponds
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: Thresholds are state‑specific adjustments to federal FPL/resource bands
mappings.review_notes: Intake uses income ranges (recipient.monthly_income_range) which are useful but too coarse for exact MSP thresholds and do not capture spouse income or countable in‑kind support.

mappings.document_name: Medicare & You — SSI and full Medicaid relationship overview
mappings.question: Is the recipient receiving SSI or likely to be eligible for SSI, which would usually confer Medicaid eligibility?
mappings.subject_and_period: Current SSI/SSDI receipt status and dates
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Are they currently receiving SSI payments? If yes, what is the most recent award date and monthly amount (or attach the award letter at application)?
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: SSI recipients generally qualify for Extra Help and are usually eligible for Medicaid; SSA award letter is primary evidence for SSI receipt.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: If recipient.current_benefits includes 'SSI' or user selects goals related to income support
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: Agency will request SSA award letter or benefits verification for application; self-report usually OK for screening
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Yes — self-report that recipient receives SSI is sufficient for preliminary identification; SSA award letter required at application for formal determinations
alternatives: Self-report for screening; SSA award letter for application
mappings.requirement_support: Medicare & You statement that SSI usually confers Medicaid and Extra Help
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: Federal program (SSI) links to state Medicaid eligibility in most states
mappings.review_notes: Intake asks current_benefits and program status; if caller selects SSI, intake supports a strong preliminary identification.

mappings.program_or_pathway: VA pension with Aid & Attendance / VA caregiver programs (PCAFC)
mappings.question: Does the veteran have a VA pension/Aid & Attendance award or a combined disability rating that triggers caregiver program eligibility?
mappings.subject_and_period: VA decision letter (most recent), combined rating percentage, pension or Aid & Attendance status
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Do you have the VA decision letter that shows combined disability rating or a VA pension/Aid & Attendance award? If not, can you check with VA/your representative?
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: VA award letters or decision letters (combined rating) and pension/Aid & Attendance determinations are the controlling documents for VA caregiver/pension pathways; specific thresholds (e.g., 70%+) and continuous care needs are program triggers.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: When case.goals includes 'Finding VA caregiver benefits' or recipient.current_benefits includes VA benefits
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: Agency/VA will require VA decision letter or pension award if applying for VA pension or caregiver benefits
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Self-report of VA benefit receipt or rating can guide preliminary routing, but the VA decision letter is required to confirm eligibility at application
alternatives: Self-report for screening; VA decision or award letter required for application
mappings.requirement_support: Not established — authoritative VA sources not retrieved in this search
mappings.retrieval_support: VA policy/documents were not retrieved; add VA resources (e.g., VHA, VBA regulations) to finalize mapping
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: VA is federal; rules and thresholds differ by program and require VA documents
mappings.review_notes: Intake contains VA-related questions but no linked official sources were retrieved — this is a coverage gap for authoritative evidence and document triggers.

mappings.document_name: (NOT RETRIEVED) California IHSS / Medi‑Cal asset transfer and lookback rules — missing source
mappings.program_or_pathway: Medi‑Cal long‑term services (including IHSS) — eligibility and transfer lookback
mappings.question: Has the recipient transferred assets in the 30‑month lookback (or state-specified period) and does that affect Medi‑Cal eligibility?
mappings.subject_and_period: Asset transfers during the preceding 30 months (or state lookback window)
mappings.proposed_followup_question: Have any assets or property been transferred, sold for less than fair market value, or given away in the last 30 months? If yes, when and what was transferred?
mappings.eligibility_rule_or_paperwork_requiremen: Medi‑Cal has transfer-of-assets rules and lookback periods that can create penalties; documentary evidence (deeds, bank transfers) may be required at application.
mappings.trigger_for_asking_fact: When recipient.living_setting indicates nursing home/skilled nursing facility or when applying for Medi‑Cal long‑term services
mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: Agency requires transfer documentation, property deeds, bank records during application if transfers reported or suspected
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Self-report of transfers is necessary for triage but insufficient to calculate penalties — documents needed for final determination
alternatives: Self-report for screening; gather deeds and transaction records for application
mappings.requirement_support: Not established — California-specific Medi‑Cal and IHSS rules not retrieved
mappings.retrieval_support: No California IHSS/Medi‑Cal documents returned in current retrieval — a coverage gap
mappings.effective_date_or_jurisdiction_notes: California-specific; retrieval of state regs required to finalize.
mappings.review_notes: Intake asks recipient.recent_transfers only for nursing home setting (show_when), but lacks follow-up detail (dates, amounts, recipient of transfer). This impedes a defensible Medi‑Cal preliminary eligibility conclusion.

mappings.document_name: (NOT RETRIEVED) SSA rules re: SSDI/SSI work credits and evidence (SSA POMS not retrieved)
mappings.program_or_pathway: SSDI / SSI eligibility (work credits, medical evidence)
mappings.question: Has the recipient worked and paid Social Security taxes sufficient to qualify for SSDI and do they meet SSA disability standards?

mappings.proposed_followup_question: Can you provide the recipient’s approximate work history (years and recent quarters when Social Security taxes were paid) or their SSA earnings record?

mappings.trigger_for_document_lookup: At application, SSA will request medical records, employer earnings, and SSA earnings history (W2s, 1099, paystubs)
mappings.is_self_report_sufficient_for_ilera_prel: Self-report of work history and existing SSA benefits is sufficient for initial triage, but SSA records/medical evidence are required later
alternatives: Self-report for screening; SSA earnings record and medical records for application verification
mappings.requirement_support: Not established — SSA source documents (POMS, regs) were not retrieved in this session

result.intake_sufficiency_assessment: The current intake supports high‑level triage and prioritization but does NOT provide all facts needed for a defensible preliminary eligibility conclusion for all pathways covered. Strengths: collects recipient health needs, living setting, coarse income ranges, benefit flags (Medicaid, SSI, VA), household size, and VA-related flags. Major gaps prevent definitive MSP or Medi‑Cal conclusions: missing Medicare Part A/B enrollment, citizenship/immigration declaration, precise income amounts and spouse income, countable resource values (life insurance cash value, burial funds), household composition for determination of eligibility unit, and state‑specific program thresholds. For VA, IHSS, SSDI/SSI, and California Medi‑Cal long‑term care specifics authoritative sources were not retrieved and intake lacks critical numeric and documentation questions. Self‑report fields allow preliminary screening in many MSP instances (CMS permits self-attestation for certain items), but ranges and missing household composition make a defensible eligibility decision impossible without follow-up or application‑level verification.
coverage_gaps: No question capturing Medicare Part A/Part B enrollment or Medicare claim number (intake missing)
No citizenship/immigration status question or signed declaration (required for MSP/Medicaid)
Income captured only as coarse ranges — missing precise gross/net monthly amounts and breakdown by household member/spouse
Assets captured as types only — missing approximate/current values and cash value of life insurance and burial funds
No detailed household composition (names/relationships/household income contributors) to define eligibility unit for MSP/Medicaid
VA documentary requirements and thresholds not retrieved — authoritative VA sources missing
California Medi‑Cal / IHSS documentation and transfer lookback rules not retrieved — state documents missing
SSA/SSI/SSDI work‑credit rules and required evidence not retrieved — SSA sources missing
Intake asks recipient.recent_transfers only when in nursing home — transfers can affect eligibility in other long‑term care contexts too
No explicit step to collect application‑level mandatory documents (SSA award letters, Medicare card, VA decision letters) though intake acknowledges some logics where 'I'm not sure' is acceptable

retrieval_queries: Medi-Cal (California) eligibility rules documentation and verification requirements; IHSS (In-Home Supportive Services) eligibility and required documents; Medicare Savings Programs (QMB, SLMB, QI) eligibility documentation and verification; Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) evidence and work credits documentation; VA Pension and Aid & Attendance eligibility documentation and rules, and VA caregiver programs (PCAFC) eligibility and required evidence; California Paid Family Leave (PFL)/State Disability Insurance (SDI) medical certification and wage deduction proof.

Supplemental Security Income (SSI) payments 
SSI provides monthly payments to adults and children who are blind or have 
a disability and have limited income and resources. SSI payments are also 
provided to people 65 and older without disabilities who meet the financial 
qualifications. These payments aren’t the same as Social Security retirement 
benefits. You may be able to get both SSI and Social Security benefits at the 
same time if your Social Security benefit is less than the SSI federal benefit 
rate. If you’re eligible for SSI, you qualify automatically for Extra Help and are 
usually eligible for Medicaid.
You can visit SSA.gov/apply/ssi to find out if you’re eligible for SSI or other 
benefits. 
Note: People who live in Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, or 
American Samoa can’t get SSI.
